To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Neto auxiliary proteins control the surface expression and synaptic incorporation of KARs, and Neto2, and Neto1 control different biophysical properties of GluK2.
Neto auxiliary subunit proteins profoundly increase the surface expression of Gluk1 receptors and also drive Gluk1 to synapses, where they are selectively incorporated into silent synaptic contacts.
Neto auxiliary proteins control GluK1 trafficking to the cell surface and to synapses, and that they also control GluK receptor properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Neto auxiliary proteins in the regulation of KAR Glu K1 receptor function and trafficking in hippocampal neurons.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the formation and plasticity of excitatory synapses in the hippocampus.
the mechanisms by which the kainate receptors (GluKs) and their auxiliary subunits, the Neto proteins, regulate excitatory synaptic transmission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Neto1/Neto2 subunit proteins regulate both the trafficking and the biophysical properties of GluK2-containing kainate receptors.
Neto proteins regulate the biophysical properties, surface expression and synaptic targeting of GluKs.
Neto auxiliary subunit proteins control both the synaptic trafficking and biophysical characteristics of GluK subfamily of KARs.

we show that Neto proteins control both the biophysical properties and trafficking of GluKs.
